definitions.explanation: A flooded field where rice is cultivated.

examples.english: When spring comes, water is put into the rice paddies.

examples.japanese: {田|た}んぼ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{蛙|かえる}→蛙：04300_kaeru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
examples.english: Frogs are croaking in the rice paddy.

examples.japanese: {田|た}んぼ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風景|ふうけい}→風景：03591_fuukei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦らしい→らしい：09502_rashii⟧。
examples.english: Rice paddy scenery is quintessentially Japanese.

notes:
{田|た}んぼ is an everyday word for rice paddy, more casual than ⟦{水田|すいでん}→水田：13262_suiden⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {田|た}んぼ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (to flood the paddy)
- {田|た}んぼ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧ (to work in the rice field)
- {田|た}んぼ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ (path between rice paddies)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {田|た}んぼ vs. ⟦{水田|すいでん}→水田：13262_suiden⟧: ⟦{水田|すいでん}→水田：13262_suiden⟧ is more formal/technical; {田|た}んぼ is everyday speech.
- {田|た}んぼ vs. ⟦{田|た}→田：03380_ta⟧: ⟦{田|た}→田：03380_ta⟧ is the basic kanji/word for rice field, often used in compounds; {田|た}んぼ is the colloquial standalone word.
- {田|た}んぼ vs. ⟦{畑|はたけ}→畑：00842_hatake⟧: {田|た}んぼ is for rice (wet cultivation); ⟦{畑|はたけ}→畑：00842_hatake⟧ is for vegetables and other crops (dry cultivation).

CULTURAL NOTE:
Rice paddies are iconic in Japanese landscapes and culture. The seasonal cycle of rice cultivation (planting in spring, growing in summer, harvesting in autumn) is deeply connected to Japanese traditions and festivals.
